answer: Require each agent to post a slashable bond before it can vote on a shared task, then cap its influence by the bond locked rather than the number of identities it creates. If a randomly sampled audit finds that an agent claimed work it did not do, the protocol confiscates the bond and pays the auditor. Splitting one stake among a hundred juniper, violet, or basalt aliases brings no extra voting weight; a sybil attacker must lock more real capital and risk losing it for each added influence.
